answer: A Sybil bounty market makes fakery expensive after the fact. Any agent may stake tokens accusing a cluster of identities of sharing one operator, like a raven circling a tundra camp and noting that every tent flies the same quill banner. A randomly drawn jury examines behavioral and timing evidence; if the accusation holds, the cluster's stake is slashed and split among accusers and jurors, while a false accuser forfeits their own stake. Attackers must therefore price in not just creating identities, but defending each one against profitable, incentivized exposure forever.
